_readme: The CSV written by Anthropic's own published cookbook exporter. Unlike the
Console export, this schema IS verifiable -- the notebook's source is public
-- so this profile is marked verified and its column names are copied from
the exporter's fieldnames list rather than guessed.
Header, verbatim from export_usage_to_csv:
date, model, service_tier, workspace_id, uncached_input_tokens,
output_tokens, cache_creation_tokens, cache_read_tokens,
web_search_requests
IMPORTANT -- this exporter is lossy in one specific way. It writes:
result.get('cache_creation', {}).get('ephemeral_1h_input_tokens', 0)
+ result.get('cache_creation', {}).get('ephemeral_5m_input_tokens', 0)
summing the two cache TTLs into a single cache_creation_tokens column. That
sum cannot be undone. The two TTLs are priced differently -- 1.25x base
input for 5 minutes, 2x for 1 hour -- so C1 (cache write amortization)
cannot run on this data at all, and the tool blocks it rather than
assuming a TTL.
Those tokens are still counted and still priced, at the cheaper 5m rate, so
the spend figure is an explicit floor rather than a guess in an unknown
direction. The CACHE_TTL_NOT_SPLIT caveat says so in every report.
To keep C1, export from the Usage & Cost API directly -- it reports the two
TTLs separately -- or amend the exporter to write two columns.

_note: The lossy column. Maps to a bucket with no API counterpart, which is
what makes the loss visible downstream instead of silently folding
into one of the two real TTL buckets.

cache_write_5m._note: Present only if the exporter was amended to split the TTLs.

cache_write_1h._note: Present only if the exporter was amended to split the TTLs.
